subject: Clarify streaming billing & tiered commit language for Atlas pilot
body_preview: Quick clarifying Qs on how streaming tokens are rounded and how commit tiers apply to pilot usage—can we codify exact metric definitions in the SOW?
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@atlas-ai.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@atlas-ai.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Billing model questions — pilot commit & streaming tokens

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Atlas is excited to proceed with a 6-week pilot. Before we sign the SOW, procurement asked for one last set of clarifications on billing. Two things came up: 

1) Streaming sessions: we plan to stream model output into our UI (frequent short responses, many concurrent connections). How do you measure "billable tokens" for streaming? Do you round per chunk/packet or aggregate per session/month? We saw notes about "streaming rounding" in the pipeline doc but need contract language.

2) Commit tiers & discounts: the SOW lists three commit tiers (50M, 250M, 1B tokens). Do discounts apply only to committed usage, or to all hosted API usage once the tier is reached that month? And how are overages priced?

Can you provide a short, contractual-ready definition we can hand to procurement + a quick example with the numbers from the SOW? If we can get final wording, procurement can circulate for signature.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 20m call if easier.

Best,
Sam Torres
Head of Product Ops | Atlas AI

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@atlas-ai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Billing model questions — pilot commit & streaming tokens

Sam — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise, contract-friendly definitions and an example using the three commit tiers in the SOW. I attached a one-page PDF and an example spreadsheet that walks the math.

Proposed metric definitions (to include in SOW / MSA):
- "Billable Token": any input or output token processed by Redwood’s Hosted API for Customer requests. Billable Tokens = InputTokens + OutputTokens (measured after tokenization using the model's tokenizer).
- "Streaming Request": any API request where tokens are returned in partial/continuous chunks over an open connection. Streaming Requests are billed based on the actual token counts produced; there is no per-connection flat fee.
- "Rounding Rules": to avoid micro-billing noise from chunking, streaming token counts shall be aggregated per Request and rounded to the nearest 0.1 token for reporting. Monthly aggregation is used for billing and rounding adjustments. Any rounding-driven overage across the billing month will be capped at 2% of total billed tokens for that month.
- "Commit Tier": a monthly committed billable token quantity in the SOW (e.g., 50M). Discounts apply to billed tokens up to the committed quantity for that month. If monthly usage exceeds the committed quantity, overages are billed at the overage rate shown in the SOW.
- "True-up": Customer and Redwood will perform a monthly true-up: billed tokens are reconciled against observed usage and invoices adjusted in the next billing cycle.

Example (from SOW numbers):
- Commit: 250,000,000 tokens/month at 20% discount vs list
- Actual month usage (after aggregation & rounding): 270,500,123 tokens
- Billed: 250,000,000 tokens at discounted rate + 20,500,123 tokens at overage rate. Any rounding overhead <= 2% is absorbed by Redwood per the Rounding Rules.

Notes / negotiation levers:
- We can tighten the rounding cap to 1% for large enterprise deals (>= 1B commit).
- If Atlas wants discounts applied to all usage once a threshold is breached (rather than only to committed quantity), we can offer that at a higher commit or as a stepped rebate.

Next steps: If this language looks OK, Laura and Markus (copied) can add legal/commercial polish and we can issue a clean SOW/DocuSign link. I attached the sample calcs.

—Priyom
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0186

Attachments: Redwood_Commit_Proposal_ATL-4721.pdf, usage_examples.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Billing model questions — pilot commit & streaming tokens

FW: Sam's procurement Qs / proposed language.

Couple of suggested edits before we publish into SOW:
1) Make the rounding unit explicit and defensible: change "nearest 0.1 token" to "nearest 0.01 token for reporting; billing rounds to the nearest 0.1 token after monthly aggregation." That lets us keep accurate telemetry without introducing penny-level invoice churn.

2) Preserve a monthly true-up window (30 days) but add a 60-day finality cutoff for disputed usage to close accounting exposure.

3) Streaming sessions with extremely short bursts (e.g., < 5 tokens per connection) can create disproportionate rounding overhead. Add an explicit cap on per-session rounding overhead: "per-session rounding overhead shall not exceed 0.5 tokens; monthly aggregated rounding overhead is capped at 2% as proposed."

4) For larger commits (>= 1B tokens), offer the alternative commercial commitment: discounts apply retroactively to all usage that month once committed quantity is reached (example: if customer hits 1B mid-month, the full month's usage is repriced at the 1B tier). This is attractive to Atlas if they prefer predictable effective rates.

5) Operationally, call out which endpoint versions / tokenizers are used for counting (we should reference the model id and tokenizer in the SOW appendix). This prevents disputes if Atlas pins different model variants during pilot.

I think once we incorporate the two rounding clarifications + the optional retroactive-reprice clause for high tiers, we can send to Sam and procurement. Markus - any objections to the 0.01/0.1 split for reporting vs billing?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Pricing & Packaging | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@atlas-ai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlas-ai.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:32:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Billing model questions — pilot commit & streaming tokens

Priyom / Laura / Markus — thanks, this is very helpful and addresses procurement's concerns. A few quick confirmations before we sign: 

- The 0.01/0.1 reporting vs billing split and the 2% monthly cap are acceptable to Atlas for the pilot.
- We'd like the 30-day true-up + 60-day dispute finality.
- We are open to the retroactive-reprice option if Redwood will include the 1B tier clause (we will aim for clarity in the SOW).

Please send the final SOW/DocuSign (with the revised wording inline) and we'll get procurement to route for signature this week. We're ready to start the pilot upon countersign.

Sam
Head of Product Ops | Atlas AI

Attachment note: we confirm receipt of "Redwood_Commit_Proposal_ATL-4721.pdf" — please include usage_examples.xlsx on the DocuSign package as an appendix for their records.
